chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn Al-Mustanir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, every worship has a period of vigor, then it becomes a period of slackness. So whoever's vigor in worship adheres to my Sunnah, he has been guided; and whoever opposes my Sunnah, he has strayed, and his deed is in ruin. Indeed, I pray and I sleep, I fast and I break the fast, I laugh and I cry. So whoever turns away from my path and my Sunnah is not from me.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Death is sufficient as an exhortation, and certainty is sufficient as wealth, and worship is sufficient as a preoccupation.'

key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: The way, tradition, or practice of the Prophet
key_terms.شِرَّةٌ: Vigor, intensity, or peak period of an activity
key_terms.فَتْرَةٌ: Slackness, lull, or period of decline

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's Sunnah in maintaining balanced worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is foundational for defining the 'Sunnah' not merely as ritualistic repetition but as a balanced, holistic way of life that integrates spiritual devotion with natural human inclinations (fitrah). It serves as a critique of both ascetic extremism and worldly negligence, establishing the Prophet’s moderate conduct as the definitive metric for authentic worship. The concluding maxims reinforce this by linking mortality to mindfulness, certainty to contentment, and worship to purposeful engagement.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Ahowl, from Sallam Bin Al Mustaneer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Indeed! Every worship has a vigour, then it comes to the nature. So the one who becomes vigorous in his worship to mysaww Sunnah, so he has been Guided, and the one who opposes mysaww Sunnah, so he has strayed, and his deeds would be in ruination. As for mesaww, Isaww pray Salāt, and sleep, and Fast, and break the Fast, and smile, and cry. So the one who turns away from mysaww Manifesto and mysaww Sunnah, so he is not from mesaww’.
And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Suffice with death as an exhortation, and suffice with the conviction as affluence, and suffice with the worship as a pre-occupation’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from al-Ahwal from Salam ibn al-Mustanir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘For every form of worship there is a strong desire and willingness, then it reduces. Whoever’ s worship falls within my tradition and practice, he has found the right guidance, and whoever is against my tradition is lost and his deeds are a total loss. I, however, pray, sleep, fast, eat, laugh and weep. Whoever dislikes my tradition and practice is not of my people.’
He has said, ‘Death is a sufficient preacher, certainty is enough wealth and worship is a complete occupation.’”
